content: The test image shows a soybean stem/root at the soil line with reddish-brown to brown discoloration and a dark lesion on the outer stem tissue. This suggests a root/stem rot disease. Top candidates: Phytophthora, Rhizoctonia, Fusarium, Pythium_damping_off.

The bottom-left of the Rhizoctonia collage looks nearly identical to the test image — same hand-holding-stem view, same reddish-brown lesion pattern at the soil line. Let me confirm by checking Fusarium.

The Rhizoctonia bottom-left reference is essentially the same view as the test image: a hand holding a soybean stem at the soil line with a reddish-brown discoloration/lesion on the outer stem tissue.

**Analysis:**
- **Affected part**: Lower stem/hypocotyl at the soil line
- **Key features**: Reddish-brown to orange-brown discoloration and dark lesion on the outer stem surface near soil level
- **Matches Rhizoctonia**: Reddish-brown lesion at the soil line on the stem — classic hypocotyl canker symptom
- **Ruled out Phytophthora**: Would show chocolate-brown discoloration extending upward multiple nodes, and wilted leaves remaining attached
- **Ruled out Fusarium**: Would show more root decay and internal vascular discoloration
